title: The first station: repentance
hookLine: the first station: regret, stopping, resolving, and making amends

lines: A LOST CAMEL IN THE DESERT.
cards: A man is crossing a waterless desert on his camel, with all his food and drink on its back. The camel wanders off. He searches until he gives up, comes to a tree, and lies down in its shade, without hope.
And then, there it is, standing right beside him, with everything still on it.
In Sahih Muslim, with a shorter version in Bukhari, the Prophet, peace be upon him, tells this story to describe how Allah meets a person who turns back to Him: more pleased than that man.

teach.b: The word is tawbah, turning back, repentance. Books of the inward path, the Revival among them, treat it as the first station. Before patience, before gratitude, before love, you turn around.
Muslim scholars describe the turn in parts. Here are four.
First, regret. A hadith says simply: regret is repentance.
It starts with honestly feeling the weight of what you did. Second, stopping. Not someday; now.
Regret while carrying on isn't the turn yet. Third, resolving not to go back. You might slip again, and the door stays open, but the intention is real.
Fourth, making amends. When the wrong touched another person, the turn isn't finished between you and Allah alone.
A report in Bukhari has the Prophet tell anyone who has wronged someone to settle it today, while it can still be settled: return what was taken, or ask to be forgiven.
That step can be the hardest, and it's very concrete: a phone call, a returned item, an apology spoken out loud.

teach.h: MORE PLEASED THAN THE MAN WITH HIS CAMEL.
teach.b: Now set the steps beside the camel story. They can sound heavy, but what waits on the other side isn't a cold ledger. It's joy.
In Pickthall's translation: "Truly Allah loveth those who turn unto Him." That's why the path puts tawbah first.
Not to shame anyone, but because every other station needs a person who has turned around and is facing the right way.

how: Muslims turn to Allah in repentance with words like astaghfirullah, and scholars describe sincere tawbah as regret, stopping the wrong, resolving not to return, and restoring the rights of anyone wronged.

o: a fee paid to a mosque so that a wrong is canceled
turning back to Allah: regret, stop, resolve, make amends
the sorrow you feel after a loss, before you heal

p: the hadith says: regret is repentance
settle it with the person, today

s: tawbah is only between a person and Allah, even when someone else was wronged
the hadith tells anyone who wronged someone to settle it today: return it, or ask forgiveness.
the Prophet compared Allah's pleasure at repentance to a man finding his lost camel
in Bukhari, Allah is more pleased than the man who finds his camel in the desert.
books of the inward path treat repentance as the first station
before patience, gratitude or love, you turn around.

games.q: you've borrowed money from a friend and never paid it back. you feel real regret. what's left to do?
o: stop, resolve, and pay it back.
games.why: when a wrong touches another person, the turn includes making it right with them, today, while it can still be settled.

practice: Let one small wrong toward a real person come to mind: a debt you didn't repay, a sharp word, a promise you dropped.

Walk it quietly through the four steps, regret without beating yourself up, stopping, resolving, and one concrete way to make it right, a message, a payment, a plain sorry, and decide when you'll do it.
If you pray, you can say astaghfirullah; if not, hold the decision steady.

wordCard.voice: Tawbah. Turning back to Allah: regret, stopping, resolving, and making amends, the first station of the inward path. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: turn back. The door stays open, and joy waits on the other side. Back tomorrow, same hill.
